bio.summary: Goldstein, also known as “Jamo,” is a first-time mayoral candidate and a CU Boulder student. His proposals include changes to housing taxation and ending the city’s Flock Safety camera contract.

statements.text: I think a Downtown Development Authority could be a useful tool for revitalizing downtown Boulder, but I do not think creating another government entity automatically fixes the problems we are facing.
statements.speaker: Jameson Goldstein
statements.source_title: Where do Boulder’s 2026 Mayorial Candidates Stand?

statements.text: I think the City’s current priorities are largely centered around long-term financial stability and our backlog of infrastructure needs, public safety and homelessness, and housing affordability.
statements.speaker: Jameson Goldstein
statements.source_title: Where do Boulder’s 2026 Mayorial Candidates Stand?

statements.text: Goldstein is running on a platform of affordability and opposition to the city’s contract with Flock Safety, which supplies Boulder’s automatic license plate readers. He proposes an excise tax on corporations that own more than 75 Boulder housing units and would use the revenue to subsidize rental assistance. He also supports keeping Boulder Municipal Airport open.
statements.speaker: Boulder Reporting Lab reporter

statements.text: Yes. Boulder needs more housing choices, especially duplexes and triplexes that can help families and middle-income resident stay here.
statements.speaker: Jameson Goldstein
statements.source_title: Where do Boulder’s 2026 Mayorial Candidates Stand?

statements.text: “Right now, there’s a very large subsection of the Boulder population that finds it very difficult to even make ends meet and pay rent,” he said.
statements.speaker: Richard Valenty reporting Jameson Goldstein’s interview

statements.text: We must cancel our Flock ‘Safety’ contract.
statements.speaker: Jameson Goldstein

statements.text: Yes. Completing the Core Arterial Network is essential to making biking, walking, and transit safer and more practical citywide.
statements.speaker: Jameson Goldstein
statements.source_title: Where do Boulder’s 2026 Mayorial Candidates Stand?
